q14.interpretation: Cards are distinct and drawn without replacement; a,b,c are ordered draw values. Real principal square roots require a>0 and bc>=0. Equality of the nonnegative left side and nonpositive right side forces bc=0. |b-c|=b-c means b>=c. For each a in {1,2,3}, valid pairs are (0,-3),(0,-2),(0,-1), and (p,0) for two positive p values other than a. Total 5 per a, hence 15 ordered triples. Original choices are 26–30; none is correct.

q24.interpretation: Let m=deg g. The strict |g(1)|<|g(2)| excludes g=0. For m>=2, deg(g-x)^3=3m is not below deg(x^2g-1)=m+2, so it cannot be the Euclidean remainder; thus deg g<=1. The divisibility gives g(1)Q(1)=g(2)Q(2)=0. Since g(2)=0 contradicts the strict inequality and Q cannot vanish at both 1 and 2 (Q has degree 1 while f^2 has degree 4), g(1)=0 and Q(2)=0. Write g=k(x-1), Q=u(x-2) with ku=4. At x=2, f(2)^2=(k-2)^3, so k>=2. Yet deg(g-x)^3<3 forces k=1, contradiction. No f,g satisfy the source conditions.
